title: Friends and friendship
description: Say what friendship is and what happens between friends.
grammar: the present tense for feelings, and the words of a quarrel
grammarNote: Say what is true now: confío en ella, discutimos a menudo, nos llevamos bien.

explanation.summary: Friendship is not only being nice to someone. It has trust, support, shared jokes and the occasional row. This unit gives you the words for all of that, so you can describe what a friend is really like.

sections.heading: What a friend gives you
sections.body: La amistad is the friendship itself, and la confianza is what you build inside it. El apoyo is the help you can count on, and la compañía is simply being together: no siempre hablamos, pero nos gusta estar juntos.

examples.es: La amistad dura más que el trabajo.

examples.en: There is a lot of trust in it.

examples.es: Te ofrece apoyo cuando lo necesitas.
examples.en: He offers you support when you need it.

sections.heading: Being with other people
sections.body: Una riña is a quarrel, and it is usually over soon: casi siempre hacemos las paces. El chiste is the joke that keeps a group together, and el grupo is the people you keep coming back to. Both nouns are masculine, except la riña.

examples.es: Tuvimos una riña, pero ya no hablamos de eso.
examples.en: We had a row, but we do not talk about it any more.
He always tells the same joke.

examples.es: El grupo de amigos queda los viernes.
examples.en: The group of friends meets on Fridays.

sections.heading: The hard part
sections.body: A friendship also has envidia. La envidia is when you want what someone else has, and a little of it can push you to do more. Discutir is to argue, and perdonar is to forgive: what goes wrong can be put right.

examples.es: Siente envidia del éxito de su hermano.
examples.en: He feels envy of his brother's success.
We argued, but we are still friends.
He asks me to forgive him.

items.note: Feminine: la compañía. It also means a company, a business.
Feminine: la riña. It takes an accent on the i.
The verb discutir: discuto, discutes, discute.
The verb perdonar: perdono, perdonas, perdona.

drills.prompt: La ___ entre ellos dura desde hace diez años.
drills.meaning: the friendship between them has lasted ten years
I have a lot of trust in my sister

drills.prompt: Hicimos las paces después de la ___.
drills.meaning: we made up after the row
he always tells the same joke
I argue a lot with my brother
drills.note: Discutir in the first person: discuto.
